Article Title: India Test squad for Sri Lanka tour likely this week; selectors sweat over Washington Sundar
Article Text:
India's Washington Sundar. (Photo by AP/PTI)

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think India will perform well in the upcoming two-Test series in Sri Lanka? Yes, they'll perform well No, it will be a tough series 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The men's senior selection committee, chaired by Ajit Agarkar , is likely to pick the squad for the upcoming two-Test tour of Sri Lanka, starting August 15 in Galle. Informal discussions took place on the sidelines of the white-ball tour in England, and a formal meeting will convene soon for the crucial series.It is learnt that the selectors are waiting for clarity on Washington Sundar, who injured himself during the three-ODI series. The all-rounder was forced to miss the series decider at Lord's and is likely to check into the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) for the necessary clearance.The official word from the Indian cricket board mentioned an injury to the right hamstring. TimesofIndia.com has learnt that while the pain subsided when he reached London, he was asked to undergo scans, which were later shared with the specialists for an opinion. It is further understood that even if it's just a pull or a Grade 1 injury, the 26-year-old could take at least two weeks to regain complete match fitness.Since the Indian squad is likely to leave for Sri Lanka as early as August 4 to commence preparations, it remains to be seen how the selectors will handle the Washington situation. The Shubman Gill-led squad will also feature in a four-day warm-up fixture before the Galle Test.The squad from the one-off Test against Afghanistan last month is set to change, as the likes of Jasprit Bumrah and Ravindra Jadeja are expected to return. It remains to be seen whether Harsh Dubey retains his spot if Washington is unable to regain fitness, or if the selectors opt for an off-spinner like Saransh Jain to maintain variety in the spin-attack.Manav Suthar and Kuldeep Yadav are likely to retain their positions, while the pace attack is expected to feature Mohammed Siraj, Gurnoor Brar and Prasidh Krishna. Jadeja wasn't picked for the fixture against Afghanistan after the IPL, but Agarkar maintained that the experienced all-rounder remains the "no. 1 spinner in the format".Regarding batting, the usual names will continue, and a decision is likely to be made on the two all-rounders Nitish Kumar Reddy and Sundar. Will the selectors opt for the seam-bowling all-rounder currently undergoing rehabilitation at the CoE, or will they look towards a specialist? These couple of calls will be interesting in what promises to be an otherwise expected squad.India have struggled in Tests under head coach Gautam Gambhir, having been whitewashed by New Zealand and South Africa at home. They need a strong series in Sri Lanka to keep their World Test Championship final qualification chances alive. After the Sri Lanka tour, India will play New Zealand, in New Zealand, before hosting Australia for five Tests at home.
Article Summary: The men's senior selection committee, chaired by Ajit Agarkar, is likely to pick the squad for the upcoming two-Test tour of Sri Lanka. Informal discussions took place on the sidelines of the white-ball tour in England, and a formal meeting will convene soon for the crucial series. It is learnt that the selectors are waiting for clarity on Washington Sundar, who injured himself during the three- ODI series.

Article Title: Shades of Diego Maradona's 1990 FIFA World Cup final in Lionel Messi's 2026 journey
Article Text:
Diego Maradona and Lionel Messi (Image credit: Agencies)

The tears took you back to a balmy July night 36 years ago. As Leo Messi stood there at the MetLife Stadium — defeated — on Sunday night, it was impossible not to be reminded of Diego Maradona . ‘El Diego’ was inconsolable as the Germans walked up to receive the World Cup at the Stadio Olimpico in Rome after their 1-0 win in the 1990 tournament.Two geniuses, two completely different characters, yet so similar in their endeavour to defend the ultimate glory their professional lives had to offer. Messi could easily have walked away after the Qatar high. Not many would have questioned Maradona either if Argentina didn’t match the dizzying heights of 1986 four years on.But they were not ready to give up. The two soldier artistes craved a return journey to the top of the world, an Odyssey of sorts, when the resources were drying up.Going into the final, just as Maradona’s Argentina were underdogs against a German side at its prime, so were Messi’s Albiceleste against La Roja that had hit its stride.A look at Argentina’s ball-possession in the two finals, too, suggest how they struggled to keep pace with their respective European opponents. On Sunday, it was a dismal 35% possession for the Argentines --the lowest by any team in a World Cup final --while the available stats say that it was 39% for Maradona’s team against the Germans.Even the red cards — Gustavo Dezotti’s ouster late in the game in 1990 — took the last fight out of the Argentines, just the way it did for the Copa America champions when Enzo Fernandez was given marching orders on Sunday. Maradona, through the 1990 World Cup, had a team that was past its prime, quite similar to Messi’s this time around. Unlike his predecessor, who couldn’t score in Italy, Messi had eight to his name this time around.But then, Maradona’s influence was massive. His assist for Claudio Cannigia brought down Brazil in the Round of 16 while the threat perception of the Argentine master didn’t allow Yugoslavia and Italy -both extremely drilled European units -to show their fangs.Just as Messi missed a penalty against Egypt in the Round of 16, Maradona, too, fluffed his lines from the spot in the tie-breaker against Yugoslavia in the quarters, only for goalkeeper Sergio Goycochea to rise to the occasion and save Argentina the blushes.The 1990 World Cup was also marked by the way Maradona divided the host country, also where he played his club football for Napoli. Before the semifinal in the stadium which is now called Diego Maradona Arena, the city of Naples was divided — one group cheering their boy while the other standing by the national colours and the Azzurri.This time, Messi’s Argentina had a similar polarizing effect over the football universe. If you believed the noise, FIFA was playing a part in the champions’ rise, while the other stood by Messi’s sorcery and the team’s incredible ability to come back, time and time again.And leading up to the final, Maradona, like Messi, was the biggest threat and German striker Juergen Klinsman explained on ESPN how they planned to neutralize the impact of the genius. “We knew one Maradona moment could finish us. Our coach Franz Beckenbauer told (defensive midfielder) Guido Buchwald to go with Diego wherever he goes, even if it is to the toilet ... Bucky clung on to Diego every minute of the game, rendering him largely ineffective. Buchwald’s persistence even earned him the surname ‘Diego’,” Klinsmann said.Times have changed, it’s no longer the era of man-to-man marking and Spain’s tactic for Messi was slightly different. It was left to Rodri and Marc Cucurella to keep him in check when he was in their zone. The idea was to isolate him and dry up the passes to him. It wasn’t before the 117th minute that Messi took his first shot at goal, which might have gone in had Mikel Merino not stood firm and take fullblooded shot to his head.Spanish coach Luis de la Fuentes’ instructions to his team to keep Messi in check were quite similar to Beckenbauer’s for his boys all those years ago “I told my players that facing Messi was the greatest challenge in football. Even at his age, he demanded our full respect from the first minute to the last. He pushed us to our absolute limit because that’s what the greatest players do,” de la Fuentes said.The inevitable happened. Ferran Torres seemed like an Andreas Brehme figure from all those years ago, putting the dagger through Argentine hearts late in the game. And once the final whistle was blown, two magicians, divided by time, stood on the same platform, tears in their eyes. Just that, they weren’t the only ones crying across the world.
Article Summary: Diego Maradona was inconsolable as the Germans walked up to receive the World Cup at the Stadio Olimpico in Rome after their 1-0 win in the 1990 tournament. The two soldier artistes craved a return journey to the top of the world, an Odyssey of sorts, when the resources were drying up.

Article Title: 'Virat Kohli aur Rohit Sharma ko touch nahi kar payenge': Ashwin makes bold statement
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli (BCCI Photo)

Rohit answers critics with Lord's century



'The noise will be there'



Poll Vote & Share your view Should selectors consider a player's historical performance in their decisions? Yes, history matters a lot No, only current form should count It should be a combination of both 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has thrown his support behind Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli , saying the two senior batters cannot simply be dropped if they still want to play for India.Ashwin's comments came after Rohit silenced retirement talk with a brilliant century in the third and final ODI against England at Lord's. Although India lost the match by 27 runs and the series 2-1, Rohit's 138 reminded everyone why he remains one of India's biggest match-winners.Speaking on his YouTube channel Ash ki Baat, Ashwin said: "'Rohit Sharma aur Virat Kohli ko touch nahi kar payenge (They will not be able to touch Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma). They cannot touch Virat and Rohit if they want to play. It is because of their credentials. Rohit has scored almost 12,000 runs; they cannot touch him."Ashwin said there was another major reason why the two stars are difficult to leave out."The other thing is, they cannot be touched because they are batters. They have an army, a battalion. People come to see them. If you drop them, it will just break the roof down."Ashwin also pointed out that bowlers do not receive the same level of public backing as star batters."But if Shami, Siraj or Bhuvneshwar are not picked, 10 people will question.100 people, 1000 people, maybe 10,000 people will question. But they won't make noise. If a day comes when people would make noise for bowlers, it would be difficult to drop them as well."Rohit's place in the ODI side had come under intense scrutiny after reports claimed that the BCCI selection committee was not considering him for the 2027 ODI World Cup.The India captain had scores of 11 and 26 in the first two ODIs against England before producing a stunning knock in the series decider.Chasing 388 at Lord's, Rohit smashed 138 off just 110 balls, hitting 17 fours and five sixes. He kept India's chase alive almost until the end, even though the visitors eventually fell 27 runs short.After the match, Rohit made it clear that speculation over his future has never affected him.In an interview with BCCI.tv, he said external criticism has always been part of his career and that his only focus is performing for India."Look, my job is with the bat... Represent my country... That's what I'm gonna do. The noise... Since I made my debut, was there and till the time I'm gonna stay here, it's always gonna be there. So it doesn't really matter too much. What matters is what I do on the field," Rohit said.
Article Summary: Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has thrown his support behind Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli. Ashwin said the two senior batters cannot simply be dropped if they still want to play for India. Rohit silenced retirement talk with a brilliant century in the third and final ODI against England at Lord's.

Article Title: 'Now you are screwing up KL Rahul, just like Sanju Samson and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi': Ex-India captain's scathing attack on team management
Article Text:
KL Rahul (Image credit: BCCI)

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe KL Rahul is better suited for the No. 4 position over No. 6? Yes, he should bat higher in the order No, No. 6 suits him better 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Former India captain Kris Srikkanth has criticised the Indian team management for sending KL Rahul in at No. 6 during the third ODI against England at Lord's. India were chasing 388 but lost the match by 27 runs, surrendering the three-match series 2-1.Sharing his views on his YouTube channel, Srikkanth questioned the decision to push Rahul down the batting order."Will anyone send KL Rahul at No.6 when chasing such a huge total? That guy has won you so much in tough run-chases," Srikkanth said."Is Rahul a No.6 or 7 batter? This is a gross injustice. His body language also looked like someone nervous," he said.Rahul walked out to bat with India at 304/4, needing almost 15 runs per over. The right-hander made 12 off eight balls before being dismissed by Jofra Archer.Srikkanth also compared Rahul's situation with the way Sanju Samson and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi were handled earlier."Just like you screwed up Sanju Samson and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, now you are screwing up KL Rahul. India needed someone to do the Jos Buttler role (the Englishman hit a 13-ball 41 in the first innings). That's where Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer got out right away. But if Rahul had gone in at No. 4, he would have complemented Virat Kohli like they did a few times in the 2023 World Cup," the 1983 World Cup winner said."Rahul is capable of accelerating easily. Instead, they sent him out to bat when the match was over. How was he possibly going to win the game needing 15 per over with Axar Patel?," Srikkanth said.Rahul featured in only two matches during the ODI series. He scored one run in the opening ODI and followed it up with 12 in the series decider at Lord's.The ODI series defeat came after India suffered a 0-4 loss in the five-match T20I series against England and a 0-2 defeat in the two-match T20I series against Ireland.India will now travel to Zimbabwe for a three-match T20I series.The first match will be played on July 23, followed by the second on July 25 and the third on July 26.All three games will be held in Harare.
Article Summary: Former India captain Kris Srikkanth has criticised the Indian team management for sending KL Rahul in at No. 6 during the third ODI against England at Lord's. India were chasing 388 but lost the match by 27 runs, surrendering the three- match series 2-1. Rahul walked out to bat with India at 304/4, needing almost 15 runs per over.

Article Title: 'Millions of immigrants parents feel proud': Inaki pens emotional tribute to brother Nico Williams after World Cup triumph
Article Text:
Nico Williams with his family

Spain's FIFA World Cup triumph was celebrated with an emotional tribute from Inaki Williams, who dedicated heartfelt words to his younger brother Nico Williams after the final.Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 to lift the trophy, adding another major title to a remarkable period of success for the country's men's and women's football teams.In a touching post, Inaki praised Nico not only for becoming a world champion but also for inspiring millions of immigrant families."You've won the World Cup. You've made history," he wrote on Instagram.He continued, "But beyond the trophy, thanks for this: you have made millions of immigrants like our parents feel proud that their future children one day can live what you have lived and that millions of Spaniards empathize with our history that is not just ours but that of all the people who leave everything behind for a better future, because you have touched the sky with your fingers and shown that with work and effort everything is possible. "Ending the message, he wrote, "Today the world has known you more if it fits and you have put our last name in infinity, for centuries and centuries. I stand in awe of you. I love you. Champion of the world."Spain's latest World Cup triumph highlights the country's dominance across all levels of football. Alongside the men's World Cup title, Spain also holds the women's world crown and has enjoyed success in European, Olympic and youth competitions.Head coach Luis de la Fuente credited the team's unity and long-term development system. "We played against the best national squads in the world, but we were the best team in the world," he said.Former France striker Thierry Henry also praised Spain's football structure, saying, "Go to work. Think about how you want to go about it at every level and play the same way. This is why they are dominating world football on every level."With young stars like Nico Williams, Lamine Yamal and Pedri leading the way, Spain's future looks just as bright as its present.
Article Summary: Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 to win the FIFA World Cup. Nico Williams' brother Inaki paid tribute to his younger brother after the final. Inaki praised Nico for inspiring millions of immigrant families. Spain's latest World Cup triumph highlights the country's dominance across all levels.

Article Title: Rs 42.3 lakh boost! Indian chess federation announces massive financial push for prodigies
Article Text:
School students hold chess board-designed placards to welcome Indian Chess grandmaster Dommaraju Gukesh after his Candidates win. (PTI Photo/R Senthilkumar)

The All India Chess Federation (AICF) has announced financial support for 42 of India's most promising young chess players, aiming to help them continue pursuing the sport without worrying about the cost of training and competition.On World Chess Day, the federation released quarterly stipends worth Rs 42.3 lakh to players in the Under-7 to Under-19 age groups, across both Open and Girls categories. The players were selected based on their performances at the 2024 National Championships, with each receiving between Rs 60,000 and Rs 1.5 lakh.Calling it a landmark step, AICF president Nitin Narang said, "Today is World Chess Day, and the All India Chess Federation (AICF) is pleased to release the another instalment of quarterly stipends, ranging from ₹60,000 to ₹1,50,000, totalling ₹42,30,000, to 42 top players across the U7 to U19 categories (Open and Girls), based on their performances in the 2024 National Championships."Highlighting the significance of the initiative, he added, "This is the first time in the history of Indian chess that our players and prodigies are receiving such financial support, so they do not have to give up their passion due to financial constraints."According to the federation, the money is meant to cover coaching and travel expenses, allowing young players to compete in international tournaments and improve their game.Narang said, "These stipends will support their coaching and travel needs, enabling them to compete globally and pursue higher goals with confidence."He also described the programme as part of AICF's long-term effort to build a stronger grassroots system, saying, "This is part of AICF's ambitious plan to create a robust ecosystem for chess in India, inspired by the vision of Aadarniya Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji to empower and encourage athletes at the grassroots."Encouraging aspiring players, he concluded, "If chess is your dream, chase it. We are with you."
Article Summary: The All India Chess Federation has announced financial support for 42 of India's most promising young chess players. The federation released quarterly stipends worth Rs 42.3 lakh to players in the Under-7 to Under-19 age groups, across both Open and Girls categories. The players were selected based on their performances at the 2024 National Championships.

Article Title: Ryan Fox hunts down history at the Open
Article Text:
Ryan Fox

Royal Birkdale (Southport): There was no dearth of drama at the 154 th Open which literally went to the wire. No less than seven players reached at least eight-under at some point and no one went past 11-under, before the roulette ball got stuck at nine-under for more than two and half hours.Then, first gingerly but surely, it slipped into the 10-under slot as New Zealand’s Ryan Fox holed the final putt from just under 12 feet to get past American Cameron Young’s clubhouse target of nine-under, which was set when Fox had not yet reached the turn in his final round.Son of former All Black rugby union international Grant Fox, the New Zealander found four birdies in his last four holes in a dramatic finish and from almost nowhere at turn, he raced past the post and opposition despite a bogey on the Par-3 15 th . With the crowd holding its breath, Fox held his nerve and putted out from 12 feet to leave Young stranded once again.Fox (68) finished 10-under, as Young (64), who rallied from three-under to nine-under, was second. Overnight leader, Sam Burns (72), who almost did not make it to the Open to be with his newborn daughter, rose to 11-under before lunging and plunging to three straight bogeys from fourth hole to fall to eightunder and stayed there till the end to be third.Defending champion Scottie Scheffler (67) never gave up till the end. He needed an impossible eagle on Par-4 18 th and ended with a bogey for a seven-under and was tied fourth with Southport born Tommy Fleetwood seeing his chances evaporate after three bogeys in a row in the middle of the round from the ninth to the 11th .
Article Summary: New Zealand's Ryan Fox holed the final putt from just under 12 feet to get past American Cameron Young’s clubhouse target of nine-under. Fox (68) finished 10-under, as Young (64), who rallied from three-under to nine- under, was second. Overnight leader, Sam Burns (72), rose to 11-under before lunging and plunging to three straight bogeys from fourth hole to fall to eightunder and stayed there till the end.

Article Title: Argentina's Emiliano Martinez makes history with record-breaking 11 saves in heartbreaking FIFA World Cup final loss against Spain
Article Text:
Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez (23) saves a shot by Spain's Nico Williams (17) during the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina.(AP/PTI)

The Stoppage-Time Miracle

Argentina may have surrendered their global crown to Spain at MetLife Stadium, but goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez etched his name into footballing record books by producing the single greatest shot-stopping performance ever witnessed in a FIFA World Cup final.Throughout 120 agonizing minutes on Sunday night, the 33-year-old custodian stood as a human wall against a relentless Spanish attack. Martínez racked up an astonishing 11 saves, the most ever recorded by a goalkeeper in a World Cup final since official data tracking began in 1966.With Argentina severely struggling to generate forward momentum—failing to register a single shot in regulation time—Spain took total command of the pitch. La Roja peppered the Argentine penalty area, unleashing continuous long-range drives and sharp box entries. Time and time again, Martínez kept the Albiceleste alive.He parried long-range rockets from Pau Cubarsí and Nico Williams, adjusted brilliantly to tip a deflected Lamine Yamal effort wide, and scrambled across his line to collect point-blank header attempts. As Argentina's outfield defensive block buckled, Martínez repeatedly bailed out his backline with heroic positioning and reflex reactions.The crowning moment of Martínez's record-setting night arrived deep into regulation stoppage time, immediately after midfielder Enzo Fernández received a red card. Faced with a dangerous 22-yard free kick from teenage prodigy Lamine Yamal, the ball curled dangerously toward the top corner. Martínez launched himself across the goal frame, producing an acrobatic fingertip save to push the ball clear and send the match into extra time.Martínez’s 11th and final save kept the scoreline deadlocked until the 106th minute, when substitute Ferran Torres finally managed to slide a strike past him into the roof of the net. While Spain walked away with the 1-0 victory and their second World Cup title, Martínez’s colossal individual performance stands alone as a landmark statistical achievement in international football history.
Article Summary: Emiliano Martínez made 11 saves, the most ever recorded by a goalkeeper in a World Cup final since official data tracking began in 1966. The 33-year-old custodian stood as a human wall against a relentless Spanish attack. Spain walked away with the 1-0 victory and their second World Cup title.

Article Title: Whopping Rs 9.6 crore! FIFA World Cup final's most expensive seats goes viral for blocked view
Article Text:
PTI Photo

Spain beat Argentina to win FIFA World Cup 2026



NEW DELHI: The FIFA World Cup 2026 final between Argentina and Spain at the New York New Jersey Stadium offered one of the most expensive tickets in sports history.FIFA's official hospitality partner, On Location, installed 12 luxury cinema-style seats right on the edge of the pitch. Each seat reportedly cost an whopping $1 million (approx INR 9.64 crore), as reported by Sport Bible.The seats gave fans a close-up view of stars like Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal, but many were left surprised after photos of the setup appeared online.Despite the huge price tag, the view from the seats was far from perfect. A thick glass barrier and photographers standing in front of the seats meant fans had an obstructed view for large parts of the match. The seats were also placed on the sunny side of the stadium, although buyers were given free sun hats.Shortly before kick-off, SportBible shared pictures of the luxury seating area."The view from the $1 million on-the-pitch seats sold by hospitality provider On Location for the FIFA World Cup Final at MetLife Stadium. It’s on the sunny side of the stadium, so sunhats are included," a SportBible journalist wrote.The pictures quickly went viral on social media.Substitute Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in extra time as Spain defeated defending champions Argentina 1-0 in the FIFA World Cup 2026 final at the jam-packed New York New Jersey Stadium.After a hard-fought 90 minutes ended without a goal, Torres broke the deadlock in the 106th minute. Nico Williams headed the ball into his path, and the Spain forward fired a powerful left-footed shot past Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez to seal the biggest win of his career.The victory gave Spain their second FIFA World Cup title and their first since lifting the trophy in South Africa in 2010.
Article Summary: FIFA's official hospitality partner, On Location, installed 12 luxury cinema- style seats right on the edge of the pitch. Each seat reportedly cost an whopping $1 million (approx INR 9.64 crore) Despite the huge price tag, the view from the seats was far from perfect.

Article Title: Indian hockey players head Down Under for Hockey One stint
Article Text:
Kanika Siwach (left) and Udita

Kolkata: Even as the Indian men’s and women’s hockey teams prepare for the upcoming World Cup and the Asian Games, a group of players outside the current national set-up has signed up to play in Australia’s Hockey One league, scheduled to be held in Oct and Nov.So far, four Indian players have officially announced their participation, all of them set to represent Melbourne Cobras franchise. The women’s contingent comprises Kanika Siwach and Udita, while Gurjant Singh and Mohammed Raheel Mouseen will feature in the men’s team. The club has also roped in former India stars Rupinder Pal Singh and Rani Rampal as ambassadors.The Cobras have been actively promoting the Indian community in Australia and have built a squad that blends Indian and Australian talent.Speaking about her decision, Kanika, daughter of former India captain and coach Pritam Siwach, said she wanted to challenge herself by stepping away from the familiarity of home.“I wanted to step out of my comfort zone. Back home, I had been with the same players for five or six years. Here, I didn’t know anyone. I had to adapt to a new culture, new teammates and a completely different environment. I wanted to test myself, and that’s why I came.”Kanika, who played in the junior World Cup last year and scored five goals, has already spent more than a month in Australia and is currently playing in the Women’s Premier League for Mentone Hockey Club.Reflecting on the experience so far, she said, “Australian hockey is very different from Indian hockey. It’s much more physical and fast-paced. They also place a huge emphasis on teamwork. In India, we focus a lot on developing individual skills, whereas here everything is more structured and team-oriented.”Udita, who has represented India in 138 internationals and last played for the national team in the Women’s World Cup Qualifiers in Hyderabad earlier this year, is equally excited about the opportunity.“Our Hockey India League is relatively short, lasting about 20 to 25 days, whereas the Australian league runs for nearly two months. That means we’ll be immersed in hockey for much longer and get to observe their training habits, routines and overall approach.”Former India drag-flicker Rupinder Pal Singh believes the stint will be invaluable for the Indian players, given the limited opportunities they get to feature in overseas leagues.“Indian players don’t often get the chance to play in international leagues, so this is a valuable opportunity,” said the former India player. “It will allow our players to experience Australian hockey culture first-hand, observe how they prepare, and learn from their training methods.”This exposure, Rupinder believes, could prove invaluable as Indian players return home with fresh ideas, different perspectives and a better understanding of one of the world’s strongest hockey systems.
Article Summary: Kanika Siwach and Udita will play for Melbourne Cobras in Hockey One league. Gurjant Singh and Mohammed Raheel Mouseen will feature in the men’s team. The club has also roped in former India stars Rupinder Pal Singh and Rani Rampal.

Article Title: Nine runs to win, 1 wicket in hand: New Zealand clinch thriller to take unassailable 3-1 lead over West Indies
Article Text:
Mitchell Santner

While much of the sporting world was focused on the FIFA World Cup final in New Jersey, New Zealand and West Indies played out a tense one-day international at Kensington Oval in Bridgetown, where both teams paid tribute to Sir Garry Sobers.New Zealand held their nerve to beat West Indies by one wicket in a low-scoring contest, taking an unassailable 3-1 lead in the five-match ODI series.Captain Mitchell Santner led the chase with an unbeaten 34, guiding the lower order through the closing stages after New Zealand looked in danger of falling short. No. 11 Jayden Lennox also played an important role, surviving 10 deliveries in an unbeaten stand of nine runs with Santner to help the visitors cross the line.Lennox had been named Player of the Match in each of the previous two games for his bowling performances.Earlier, Mark Chapman top-scored for New Zealand with 80 after West Indies were bowled out for 188 on a two-paced surface.With three runs needed and one wicket remaining, Santner was dropped before Lennox survived reviews for both a caught-behind and an lbw appeal. New Zealand eventually reached the target with 35 balls to spare.“It was pretty chaotic, especially the ending,” Santner said. “You try to chip off the total as much as you can. Even partnerships of 10 or 15 at that stage was going a long way.“It probably shouldn't have got that close but it was nice to get over the line.”The match was played two days after the death of Sir Garry Sobers, who died on Friday at the age of 89. Playing in Sobers' hometown of Bridgetown and at Kensington Oval, where he built his career, West Indies had hoped to honour one of the country's greatest cricketers with a victory.Both teams wore black armbands, flags flew at half-mast, two seats in the Sir Garry Sobers Pavilion were left empty, and a minute's silence was observed before the start of play.Sobers is widely regarded as the greatest West Indies cricketer and one of the finest all-rounders in the history of the game, scoring more than 8,000 Test runs and taking over 200 wickets.West Indies' hopes of a fitting tribute suffered an early setback when New Zealand won the toss and chose to bowl. Teams batting second have now won all four matches in the series.The home side slipped to 58 for 3 and then 81 for 6 before Amir Jangoo and Gudakesh Motie added 81 runs for the seventh wicket to revive the innings.Jangoo scored 51 from 71 balls, while Motie contributed 41 to take West Indies to 188.Young fast bowler Matthew Fisher claimed 3 for 40, his first ODI wickets for New Zealand.
Article Summary: New Zealand hold their nerve to beat West Indies by one wicket in a low-scoring contest. Captain Mitchell Santner led the chase with an unbeaten 34, guiding the lower order through the closing stages. The match was played two days after the death of Sir Garry Sobers, who died on Friday at the age of 89.

Article Title: India at CWG 2026: Know Your Athlete - ​​Neeru Pathak (Athletics)
Article Text: Event: Women's 400 metres, Mixed 4 x 400 metres relayCWG Record: The 19-year-old Indian sprinter earned her first-ever selection to the Indian athletics contingent for the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.Personal bests: 52.78 in Women's 400 metres, 3:17.06 in Mixed 4 x 400 metres relayNeeru Pathak will be one of the youngest members of India's athletics team at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. At 19, she has earned her first selection to the Indian contingent and will compete in the women's 400 metres as well as the mixed 4x400 metres relay.The young sprinter has made steady progress over the past year and has already begun collecting medals at the international level. Article Title: Bhola elected Hockey Jharkhand president for fourth term on trot
Article Text:
Bhola Nath Singh

Kolkata: Hockey India secretary general Bhola Nath Singh was on Sunday elected unopposed as Hockey Jharkhand president for a fourth consecutive term during the association’s 13th Annual General Meeting in Ranchi.The election, however, comes amid a legal challenge over Singh’s eligibility to continue in office.The National Sports Governance Act, 2025 states that “a person may continuously hold the position of either the president or the secretary general or the treasurer, as the case may be, for up to three consecutive terms separately, or in combination thereof”.Hockey Jharkhand, however, maintained that Singh’s re-election was in accordance with the National Sports Policy 2025, which Hockey India has implemented.In its official release, the association stated that “owing to being an office-bearer in an international sports federation, Bhola Nath Singh was elected Hockey Jharkhand president for a fourth consecutive time”.Besides serving as Hockey Jharkhand president and Hockey India secretary general, Singh has also been the vice-president of the Asian Hockey Federation (AHF) since his election to the post in March 2023.Meanwhile, Manoj Kumar Prasad was elected unopposed as general secretary, while Asrita Lakra was elected treasurer.The development comes days after a group of 13 former international and national hockey players served a legal notice to Hockey Jharkhand and the Jharkhand Sports Department, questioning the legality of the election process. Several of the petitioners including Sumrai Tete, along with former India women’s captain Asunta Lakra, staged a peaceful protest outside the venue carrying placards, but did not make any public statements.During the AGM, Hockey Jharkhand also ratified its annual accounts and reports for 2025-26 and distributed sports kits worth ₹65,000 each to 20 districts as part of its grassroots development programme.
Article Summary: Bhola Nath Singh was on Sunday elected unopposed as Hockey Jharkhand president for a fourth consecutive term. The election, however, comes amid a legal challenge over Singh’s eligibility to continue in office. Singh has also been the vice-president of the Asian Hockey Federation (AHF) since his election to the post in March 2023.

Article Title: India's bowling lacks bite without Jasprit Bumrah; middle-over planning all over the place
Article Text:
Cardiff [Wales], Jul 16 (ANI): India's Jasprit Bumrah during a warm-up session before the 2nd ODI against England, at Sophia Gardens stadium in Cardiff on Thursday. (ANI Photo)

TimesofIndia.com in London

Poll Vote & Share your view What factor contributed the most to India's loss in the third ODI? Bumrah's absence Poor middle overs bowling Too many extras 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

: Jacob Bethell and Ben Duckett went about a warm, pleasant and sunny morning at the Lord's Cricket Ground on Sunday with some ease. Having won the toss, the duo started slowly but picked up pace as the day went on in the third ODI against India. Arshdeep Singh and Prasidh Krishna took the new ball duties with Jasprit Bumrah unavailable due to an impact injury on his left knee during the second ODI. Reactive swelling on his left knee put India's premier seamer on the sidelines, with Arshdeep taking his spot in the series decider.Krishna plugged the gaps with back-to-back maiden overs as he found his line, length and extra bounce. A streak of 20 dot balls defined the 30-year-old's day out. Unfortunately, with Bumrah not there to aid the effort on the other side, and no one chipping in remotely close to what 'Boom' offers, the struggle to find a wicket or apply pressure by stemming the flow of runs continued.Prince Yadav, coming in as a replacement for the injury-affected Washington Sundar, playing just his third ODI, started by going for 11 runs, including a massive wide that evaded a desperate dive from wicketkeeper Ishan Kishan.If the placid bowling wasn't enough, the extras further played into England's hands. India gifted away 26 extras, including 16 in wides and nine in leg byes."That about sums up India's bowling and day so far," chimed former England captain Nasser Hussain in commentary as Prince Yadav's length delivery on the pads in the 28th over was tickled towards fine leg by Bethell for a boundary. "India will be very disappointed with their bowling today; they've been very ordinary," admitted Ravi Shastri not long after.A 192-run stand between Bethell and Duckett ticked off multiple record boxes. It was England's first century-stand in ODIs since 2023. It was England's biggest stand against India in an ODI. At Lord's, it was the first ton-up stand for the hosts since 2010. It was also the biggest first-wicket partnership at the iconic venue ever.Before Duckett fell to Prince Yadav, scoring 141 off 135 balls, he jotted down milestones of his own. None bigger, possibly, than overhauling Viv Richards' record for the highest score at this venue (138) back in the 1979 World Cup final.England racked up 387/3 on the board -- the biggest ODI score at Lord's since the first-ever World Cup in 1975 -- a day made more famous by Sunil Gavaskar's 174-ball 36 in a 335-run chase.Unlike Gavaskar, Root, another legend of the game, opted for a brisk showing, scoring an unbeaten 48-ball 74. A sixth straight ODI fifty for Root, whom India failed to dismiss even once in the 50-over series. Root amassed 249 runs in three innings and India barely even got close to getting him out.The damage was done by the first-wicket partnership, exacerbated in the middle overs, and the result was all but confirmed in the end. The power play went for 58; the middle overs produced 203/1 and the final 10 overs saw 126 runs, including 62 runs in the last three.Not surprisingly, the bowlers bled runs. Gurnoor Brar conceded 97, Prince another 79, Arshdeep went for 72, and even Prasidh, the pick of the bowlers with two wickets, conceded 69 runs - most of them coming in the slog overs.On a surface that offered support to seamers when there was disciplined bowling, as displayed by Prasidh's dot-ball spell, India were erratic and paid for it. The Men in Blue fielded five frontline bowlers and desperately missed Bumrah while also, once again, deciding to keep Kuldeep Yadav on the bench.The wrist spinner has been involved in just eight ODIs out of the 15 played by the side since India's successful Champions Trophy campaign. His ability to provide breakthroughs in the middle overs has been crucial to India's winning formula. Yet, as India struggle to control the flow of runs and eke out a wicket during that passage, he has not been brought in.The 31-year-old was involved in all three net sessions at Edgbaston ahead of the first ODI and was also busy in the optional session before the series-deciding third. As Sundar picked up an injury, Kuldeep was believed to be the ideal change. Alas, that wasn't to be the case."If you're a side that's able to take wickets through that middle period of the game, it puts you in such a strong position going into the back end of the game. Likewise with the bat, if you're a strong enough side to be able to rotate and pick up boundaries here and there as a batting unit, it sets you up going into the last 10 overs, which can have a massive impact on the game," said England skipper Harry Brook ahead of the third ODI.India, unfortunately for their 2027 ODI World Cup title hopes, haven't challenged consistently in these middle overs. Against New Zealand in three ODIs, the middle overs saw: 163/5, 193/2 and 191/1. That scenario improved against Afghanistan before, once again, looking dire against England: 152/6, 146/4 and 203/1.India's seam bowling effort without Bumrah looked uninspired and insipid. The day out at Lord's appeared more a case of Sunday cricket with the bowlers going about their motion without much of a thought involved. The bulk of the deliveries landed full and were duly dispatched for 105 runs. At the other end of the surface, India seamers bowled 38 short balls and were whacked for 87 runs, going at an economy rate of 13.73. When the bowlers did get their line right, on 77 balls, they let go of 58 runs.Ultimately, the 388-run target proved to be a bridge too far. It was a consequence of more than just one poor outing. Bumrah's absence exposed the lack of bite in the pace attack, but the larger concern, perhaps, remains India's inability to seize control through the middle overs.While England's batters executed their plans with clarity, India were left searching for answers, persisting with combinations that have repeatedly failed to stem the flow of runs. With 15 months to go before the 2027 ODI World Cup, these recurring issues are becoming less about experimentation and more about missed opportunities to settle on a bowling formula that can consistently take wickets, apply pressure and win matches.
Article Summary: Jacob Bethell and Ben Duckett put on 192 for the first-wicket partnership. England racked up 387/3 on the board, the biggest ODI score at Lord's since 1975. Jasprit Bumrah missed the third ODI due to an impact injury on his left knee.

Article Title: 'Messi took us to top of the world': Fans pack Buenos Aires streets to applaud Argentina's World Cup campaign despite final loss - Watch
Article Text:
Fans gather during the World Cup final match between Argentina and Spain in downtown Buenos Aires, Argentina, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo)

ALSO READ:

Is there a more devoted fanbase in international football than Argentina's? Sunday's scenes after the FIFA World Cup 2026 final defeat to Spain once again made that question difficult to answer.Rather than leaving in silence after the 1-0 extra-time loss, Argentina supporters stayed back to cheer their team. They sang their football anthems, chanted "Messsiii, Messsiii" around the stadium and applauded the players long after the final whistle.The same emotion was visible thousands of kilometres away in Buenos Aires, where supporters gathered around the city's Obelisk to thank the team despite the defeat. Their message was simple: "Gracias iguales."Fans had held on to hopes of another comeback until the final whistle. But once Spain sealed victory, disappointment gradually gave way to appreciation for a campaign that had once again taken Argentina to the World Cup final.At the Obelisk, the traditional meeting point for football celebrations in the Argentine capital, supporters who had assembled hours before kick-off first stood in silence before breaking into songs in honour of the team."We reached the final, and that's no small achievement," said 20-year-old student Luciano Ortega with a smile, as quoted by Buenos Aires Times.As the evening progressed (local time), more fans poured into the square. Drums, fireworks, firecrackers and car horns filled the air as supporters continued chanting despite the result.Argentina President Javier Milei also praised the team, posting on X: "Thank you very much, players! You fought until the very end. Argentina always at the top."In Rosario, Lionel Messi 's hometown about 300 kilometres northwest of Buenos Aires, hundreds gathered at the Monumento Nacional a la Bandera to salute the team after the final.The monument was lit in Argentina's national colours as supporters waved flags, wore national team shirts and held photographs of Messi while fireworks lit up the night sky."We've already won a World Cup. We shouldn't just cry, we should celebrate. Messi already took us to the top of the world," Sergio Irrazábal, who attended with his family wearing a light-blue-and-white wig, told AFP.South American football governing body CONMEBOL also acknowledged the scenes, posting a video of the celebrations on X with the caption: "Despite the result, Argentina valued its team's campaign."Spain's victory gave them their first World Cup title since 2010 and extended Luis de la Fuente's side's unbeaten international run to a European-record 38 matches.For Argentina, the defeat ended an impressive title defence that began after lifting the trophy in Qatar four years ago. It also came in what is widely expected to be Lionel Messi's final appearance at a World Cup.Even after the defeat, the mood across Buenos Aires reflected pride more than disappointment. Supporters chose to celebrate a team that reached another World Cup final and remained in the contest until Ferran Torres scored the extra-time winner that settled the match.
Article Summary: Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain in the FIFA World Cup 2026 final on Sunday. Despite the defeat, Argentina supporters stayed back to cheer their team. Supporters gathered around the Obelisk in Buenos Aires to thank the team. Argentina President Javier Milei also praised the team on Twitter.

Article Title: It felt like standing before God: Yastika Bhatia on her emotional Lord’s century

Never easy to come back after a surgery: Yastika’s mom Garima

From a career-threatening ACL injury to her left knee that sidelined her for more than 18 months to becoming the first woman cricketer to score a Test century at Lord’s, Yastika Bhatia’s return to competitive cricket has been nothing short of inspirational. On Saturday, the wicketkeeper-batter from Vadodara, who scored a match-winning 113 off 158 balls against England recently, was felicitated by Baroda Cricket Association (BCA). Speaking to us on the sidelines, Yastika opened up about her century, her time away from the game, the conversation with Smriti Mandhana that gave her a much-needed mental boost, and more. Excerpts:Very few cricketers get the opportunity to score a century at Lord’s, and it’s a very special feeling. I did not have a very good T20 World Cup, and I was hungry for runs. It was not an easy wicket to bat initially, and I just told myself that I needed to stay out there. I was not out on 39 when the day’s play ended, and I told myself, ‘61 runs.’ The next day, I was not out on 91 at lunch, so I was both nervous and excited. Initially, I kept thinking about how I would celebrate once I reached the milestone, but then I told myself not to think about anything until I actually got there. The moment I took that single and completed my hundred, I became very emotional. Everything I had gone through over the last two years came rushing back. A couple of months ago, I visited the Mahakal Temple and felt a powerful divine energy. As I stood there soaking in the applause at Lord’s, it felt almost the same—BhagwanI just thanked God, my family and all my well-wishers for their faith in me.When I got injured, it was a huge blow as I was eager to play in the home World Cup (2025 ODI WC). Kiran More, who always tells me that I am his best student, came home and assured me that things would be fine. He said, “time” and his positivity was very reassuring. Due to muscle loss, I had to start from scratch again but during that phase, I focused on being a good student of the game. Even when you are not playing, you can learn a lot by just observing. And once I resumed practice after so many months, I fell in love with cricket all over again. These few months have taught me the value of patience and resilience.I still remember the day when my teammates got to know that I would miss the ODI World Cup due to injury. They were crying. However, talking to Smriti(Mandhana) gave me a lot of strength. She had a similar injury in 2017 but has played her best cricket after making a comeback. She told me, “Don’t worry, it will be the turning point of your career. You will learn a lot about the game and life while you are away for rehab”. Amol (Muzumdar) sir (Team India coach), Harry (Harmanpreet Kaur)and all the seniors would always be in touch and tell me, “, you will be back in the team soon.” That kind of support meant a lot and motivated me.Vadodara has played a huge role in my journey, and I am grateful to the Baroda Cricket Association (BCA) for their constant support. It has been the backbone of my career. I remember when I started doing well for Team Baroda, Rajkuvardevi (Geeta) Gaekwad (former Indian cricketer from the city) always said, “Radha (Yadav) and Yastika will play for India soon; they have it in them.” I am also grateful to my coach Santosh Chaugule and mentor Kiran More for always being there. It was a huge moment to find my name on the Lord’s honours board and every time I do well, I thank the city’s contribution in my journey. I hope this is just the beginning; IndiamatchesI hope I can do well for India in big tournaments like the World Cup and Champions Trophy. Women’s cricket is a part of the 2028 Olympics, and my goal is to make sure that I am a part of that team. It would be such a great achievement if we can win an Olympic gold for the country! Now that there’s pay parity and our match fees are on par with the men’s team, parents see cricket as a viable career option for young girls. With Team India continuing to perform well, many more girls are inspired to take up the sport, and that’s a very encouraging sign. The BCCI and ICC deserve credit for promoting women’s cricket well, and I am also grateful to the media for their constant support.After the injury, Yastika had to undergo surgery, and she moved to the BCCI’s Centre of Excellence (COE) in Bengaluru for rehab. Garima Bhatia, her mom, went to Bengaluru and stayed with Yastika for almost the entire duration. She tells us, “It’s never easy to come back after surgery and initially, Yastika would feel very low. Her dream of playing in a home World Cup (the 2025 ODI World Cup) had been shattered due to this injury. We are grateful to the COE and BCCI for taking such excellent care of her. Her teammates and coaches were very supportive too, and slowly, she started feeling better. I am proud of the way she has come back and scored a Test century.”
Article Summary: Yastika Bhatia is the first woman cricketer to score a Test century at Lord’s. The wicketkeeper-batter from Vadodara was felicitated by Baroda Cricket Association (BCA) She opened up about her century, her time away from the game, the conversation with Smriti Mandhana that gave her a much-needed mental boost.

Article Title: After England Test axe, Brendon McCullum to be 'around for The Hundred' to scout white-ball talent
Article Text:
Brendon McCullum (AP Photo)

White-Ball Success Shapes New Role



'Give and Take' Between Red and White Ball

Former England Test head coach Brendon McCullum has confirmed he will remain in England throughout The Hundred to closely monitor the country's emerging white-ball talent, signalling a complete shift in focus to his role as England's limited-overs coach.McCullum's decision comes just days after the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) relieved him of his Test coaching duties following England's 2-1 home Test series defeat to New Zealand. The loss extended England's poor red-ball run to seven defeats in their last nine Tests, prompting the ECB to split the coaching responsibilities.Instead of returning to his native New Zealand, McCullum will spend the next four weeks travelling across England to watch The Hundred, identifying players capable of strengthening England's ODI and T20I squads.The move reflects his renewed commitment to England's white-ball setup, which has enjoyed an impressive resurgence under his guidance. England recently completed a 4-0 T20I series sweep and secured a 2-1 ODI series victory over world champions India, reinforcing the ECB's decision to retain him as the white-ball coach."I'll be around for The Hundred, I think it'd be great to see some of England's premier white-ball tournament.If you're the white-ball coach, I think it's good to be around for that, seeing not just the guys who are in this squad, but also some of the next talent perform under the brightest lights of The Hundred tournament,'' McCullum said as per Cricinfo."I think it'd be good to be able to see that up close over the next four weeks or so. I'll look to try and get around some of those games and see that, and hopefully we'll see some more talent," he added.McCullum acknowledged that balancing player workloads between the two formats would require cooperation, saying there must be "give and take" between the white-ball and Test setups to ensure the long-term success of English cricket."Collaboratively, I think," McCullum answered when asked how he saw the sharing of resources with the future Test coach."Once the new coach is put in place, I think we'll have a good conversation around everything. Ultimately, as long as everyone wants what's right for English cricket, then there'll be some give and take on certain things, and that's just the way it is,'' McCullum added.
Article Summary: Former England Test head coach Brendon McCullum will remain in England throughout The Hundred to closely monitor the country's emerging white-ball talent. McCullum's decision comes just days after the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) relieved him of his Test coaching duties following England's 2-1 home Test series defeat to New Zealand.

Article Title: Kemar Roach to be honoured by CWI after historic 300-Test wicket milestone

Cricket West Indies (CWI) will honour veteran Barbadian pacer Kemar Roach for reaching the remarkable milestone of 300 Test wickets with a special on-field presentation at Kensington Oval on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, during the fifth ODI between West Indies and New Zealand.Roach etched his name into West Indies cricket history by becoming only the fifth West Indian and the second Barbadian to claim 300 Test wickets. It is a richly deserved honour, and one that reflects the profound impact he has made on West Indies cricket," CWI President Dr.Kishore Shallow said in a statement.Since making his Test debut against Bangladesh in 2009, Roach has been the cornerstone of the West Indies pace attack, earning a reputation for his outstanding control, late swing, and relentless accuracy. Across his illustrious Test career, the 38-year-old has claimed 300 wickets at an average of 28.83, including 12 five-wicket hauls and one 10-wicket match haul, cementing his place among the finest fast bowlers in West Indies cricket history.
Article Summary: Kemar Roach becomes only the fifth West Indian and the second Barbadian to claim 300 Test wickets. He achieved the landmark during the West Indies' innings victory over Sri Lanka. A special on-field presentation will take place during the fifth ODI between West Indies and New Zealand.

Article Title: BCCI adopts MCC rule changes for 2026-27 domestic season; final over to continue even if wicket falls
Article Text:
Logo of BCCI (PTI Photo)

Other rule changes:

Mumbai: In line with the rule changes recommended by the Lord's-based Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) recently, the BCCI has made changes to its playing conditions for the 2026-27 domestic season, as per which the final over of the day will have to be completed even if a wicket falls during the over.According to a note (TOI has a copy) on the playing conditions for the upcoming season, circulated by the BCCI to the state associations, the BCCI has stated that as per the MCC rules, the final over of the day must be completed regardless of a wicket fall.As per clause 12.5.2, "The final over of a day's play will now be completed even if a wicket falls during it."The MCC's reason for the change mentions, "Significant change for multi-day cricket. Prevents batting sides from avoiding sending a new batter out late in the day." This playing condition, of course, concerns the multi-day (red-ball) format.The BCCI's 15-page note called Summary of Changes to the Playing Conditions - 2026-27 - to the state associations, mentions, "The 2026 edition (4th edition of the 2017 Code of Laws) changes whichever are applicable, all gendered language (he/she, him/her, etc.),other relevant changes as discussed in BCCI are being incorporated while drafting this year's playing conditions."A significant change, triggered by the MCC's changed rules, is that a bowler deliberate front-foot no-balls and deliberate non-landing deliveries will now be barred from bowling for the rest of the match, rather than just the innings.The proposed rule change to the playing conditions (41.8) is: "Bowler suspended for deliberate front foot no ball cannot bowl in the whole match." As per an explanation by the MCC: "Penalties for deliberate front foot no ball now apply to the whole match, not just an innings."As per the changed rule, declaration and forfeiture is no longer permitted in the final innings of the match. The MCC's reasoning is that, "This was only used for contrived results and was felt to be bad for the game."- During One-dayers, the head coach will be permitted to enter the field during drinks intervals during ODIs.- Abandoning a run without intent to deceive is not a deliberate short run. The batters can turn back and abandon a run even after crossing.- Fielding captain decides which batter faces next if obstruction prevents a catch.- The ball is 'finally settled' if it is in the hands of any fielder or stationary on the ground. The ball no longer needs to be with the bowler or keeper to be 'Dead'. It gives umpires more reasonable leeway.- A guideline for the leg side wide in One-day and T20 games, for clarity.- All fielders must be within the boundary at the moment the ball is delivered. It enshrines the idea that play happens within the boundary and closes a loophole for leg-side restrictions.- The wicket-keeper must be behind the wicket from 'instant of delivery' instead of 'moment ball in play'. The keeper is no longer punished for having gloves in front during the run-up.- Umpires must prevent further use of illegal equipment and report it. The changed rule clarifies It is the responsibility of the umpires to prevent repeated use of illegal equipment.
Article Summary: The BCCI has made changes to its playing conditions for the 2026-27 domestic season. The final over of the day will have to be completed even if a wicket falls during it. Article Title: Nathan Smith, Danni Wyatt-Hodge crowned ICC Players of the Month for June 2026
Article Text:
Nathan Smith, Danni Wyatt-Hodge crowned ICC Players of the Month (Image: X)

Nathan Smith shines in historic Test series win



Wyatt-Hodge rewarded after record-breaking World Cup campaign



New Zealand fast bowler Nathan Smith and England opener Danni Wyatt-Hodge have been named the ICC Men's and Women's Players of the Month for June 2026 following their outstanding performances in international cricket. The International Cricket Council (ICC) announced the monthly awards on Monday, recognising the duo for their match-winning displays in Test and T20I cricket respectively.Smith beat India captain Shubman Gill and Bangladesh all-rounder Mosaddek Hossain to claim the men's honour, while Wyatt-Hodge finished ahead of India's N Sree Charani and Scotland captain Kathryn Bryce to secure the women's award.Smith played a pivotal role in New Zealand's remarkable 2-1 Test series triumph over England away from home. Leading an inexperienced bowling attack, the right-arm pacer finished as the series' highest wicket-taker with 16 wickets at an average of 23.00. His defining performance came at Lord's, where he produced a sensational match haul of 9/132, including 6/70 in the second innings, helping New Zealand register a memorable victory and lay the foundation for their series comeback.Reacting to the award, Smith said the recognition was special but insisted the team's success remained his biggest achievement."This is really special. It was a great tour of England for the boys, and this is pretty cool. I don't usually play for individual awards, but it's nice to receive this recognition and, more importantly, to have contributed to a series win," Smith said.England opener Danni Wyatt-Hodge claimed her second ICC Player of the Month award after starring in the ICC Women's T20 World Cup on home soil. The experienced batter finished the tournament's league stage as the highest run-scorer, accumulating 302 runs. Wyatt-Hodge produced a brilliant 105 off 62 balls against Sri Lanka*, followed by an unbeaten 89 off 53 deliveries against defending champions New Zealand. She was named Player of the Match in both encounters, underlining her consistency throughout the tournament.Reflecting on the honour, Wyatt-Hodge said the recognition made an unforgettable World Cup campaign even more memorable."I'm delighted to win the ICC Player of the Month award, especially since it came for performances at a World Cup on home soil. The ICC Women's T20 World Cup was a fantastic occasion for the game, and having the opportunity to play in the final at Lord's is a memory that my teammates and I will cherish forever," she said.
Article Summary: New Zealand fast bowler Nathan Smith and England opener Danni Wyatt-Hodge named ICC Men's and Women's Players of the Month for June 2026. The International Cricket Council (ICC) announced the monthly awards on Monday, recognising the duo for their match-winning displays in Test and T20I cricket respectively. Smith beat India captain Shubman Gill and Bangladesh all-rounder Mosaddek Hossain to claim the men's honour. Wyatt- Hodge finished ahead of India's N Sree Charani and Scotland captain Kathryn Bryce to secure the women's award.

Article Title: Ashutosh Sharma, owner of India's fastest T20 fifty joins Hampshire for One-Day Cup
Article Text:
Delhi Capitals' batter Ashutosh Sharma (PTI Photo)

English county side Hampshire have strengthened their squad for the upcoming Metro Bank One-Day Cup by signing Indian all-rounder Ashutosh Sharma, the club confirmed on Monday. The 27-year-old, who represents Delhi Capitals in the Indian Premier League (IPL), will join Hampshire for the duration of the 50-over competition. Delhi Capitals are co-owned by GMR Group , which also owns Hampshire, making the move a natural fit.Ashutosh has earned a reputation as an explosive middle-order batter in the IPL. Across the last two seasons, he has accumulated more than 375 runs for Delhi Capitals while maintaining an impressive strike rate of 170 and an average of 31.25.The hard-hitting batter also holds a remarkable domestic record. During the 2023 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, he blasted a half-century in just 11 deliveries for Railways against Arunachal Pradesh, setting the record for the fastest T20 fifty by an Indian.Welcoming the signing, Hampshire's Director of Cricket Giles White expressed confidence in the Indian's abilities."We're delighted to bring Ashutosh to Hampshire for the One-Day Cup.He's a talented cricketer who has shown his quality in the IPL with Delhi Capitals and understands what it takes to perform at a high level. We're excited to have him in our squad and hope he can help us go one better in this year's competition," White said.Ashutosh has also built a solid domestic record in List A cricket, scoring 458 runs in 21 matches. He made his domestic debut for Madhya Pradesh in 2017 before moving to Railways, where he currently plays. Across all formats, he has featured in 91 domestic matches.In IPL, Ashutosh was first picked up by Punjab Kings. He made his league debut as an Impact Substitute and smacked 31 off 17 balls, before being signed by Delhi Capitals for INR 3.80 crore ahead of IPL 2025.
Article Summary: Hampshire sign Indian all-rounder Ashutosh Sharma. Sharma currently plays for Delhi Capitals in the Indian Premier League. The 27-year-old will join Hampshire for the duration of the 50-over competition. Delhi Capitals are co-owned by GMR Group, which also owns Hampshire.

Article Title: R Ashwin points to selection bias, explains why Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli are 'impossible to drop'
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli (Image: AP)

'No-one can touch Virat or Rohit'





Ashwin raises voice for bolwers

Former India off-spinner Ravichandran Ashwin believes dropping senior stars Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli is virtually impossible as long as they want to continue playing, citing their extraordinary achievements and immense fan following.Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli have been the pillars of Indian cricket for over 15 years, and as long as they continue to perform, leaving them out of the national team is far from straightforward. While opportunities should be created for the next generation, former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin believes the duo enjoy a level of protection that bowlers rarely receive.Ashwin argued that star batters like Rohit and Virat command unparalleled influence because of their achievements and massive fan following, whereas bowlers such as Mohammed Shami and Mohammed Siraj are more vulnerable to being dropped despite their contributions.Siraj last represented India in the Test against Afghanistan on June 6, 2026, in New Chandigarh, while Shami's most recent international appearance came in the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 final against New Zealand in Dubai.Speaking on his YouTube channel, 'Ash Ki Baat', Ashwin said dropping Rohit is not as simple as leaving out any other player, particularly after the veteran opener's recent performances. He also highlighted the long-standing disparity in Indian cricket, where star batters often receive greater backing and recognition than bowlers."No one will be able to touch Virat or Rohit if they want to continue playing because both have incredible credentials. Rohit has more than 12,000 international runs, and both of them have consistently delivered for India. They are batters, and they have massive fan armies. People come to the stadiums to watch them. If you drop either of them, the noise will be deafening," Ashwin said on his YouTube channel, Ash Ki Baat.Ashwin contrasted that with the treatment of bowlers."If Shami isn't picked, or Siraj isn't picked, or Bhuvneshwar isn't picked, maybe 10 people will ask questions, then 100, 1,000 or even 10,000 at most. But it won't create the same uproar. That's the difference. If bowlers also started receiving that kind of support, they too would become undroppable. But the reality is that dropping Virat or Rohit is almost impossible," he added.
Article Summary: Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli have been pillars of Indian cricket for over 15 years. Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin believes the duo enjoy a level of protection that bowlers rarely receive. Ashwin said dropping Rohit is not as simple as leaving out any other player, particularly after the veteran opener's recent performances.

Article Title: 'He has shut up everybody': Ravi Shastri defends Rohit Sharma after Lord's century
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma plays a shot during 3rd ODI against England at Lord's. (ANI Photo)

'Rohit didn't need to prove' - Ravi Shastri

'My job is to bat' - Rohit Sharma

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think Rohit Sharma should continue playing despite retirement rumors? Yes, he should decide his own timing No, it's time for him to retire 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Former India head coach and commentator Ravi Shastri has backed Rohit Sharma amid retirement speculation, urging the team management to allow the veteran opener to continue playing for as long as he wants following his historic century at Lord's.Rohit silenced his critics in emphatic fashion by smashing a magnificent 138 off 110 balls in the third ODI against England at the Home of Cricket. The innings saw him become the first Indian batter to score an ODI century at Lord's, coming at a time when speculation was rife that the match could be his final international appearance before the 2027 ODI World Cup.The retirement rumours had earlier been dismissed by the BCCI , and Rohit responded in the best possible way, with a record-breaking knock.Reacting to the veteran batter's performance, Shastri said Rohit has nothing left to prove and should be allowed to decide the timing of his own retirement."He (Rohit Sharma) didn't need to prove himself, but he has shut up everybody. But if he has the desire to play, work hard at his game, and is still enjoying it, I think he should be given the opportunity for as long as he wants.The day will come when he feels he doesn't have it in him anymore, and he'll go," Shastri told Sky Cricket.Rohit's innings was his 34th ODI century and his maiden hundred at Lord's. Despite his heroics, India fell 27 runs short in their chase of 388, handing England a 2-1 ODI series victory.Speaking to bcci.tv after the match, Rohit made it clear that external criticism has never affected his mindset, insisting his only focus is helping India succeed."Look, my job is with the bat, to come out, play, represent my country and represent the team. That's what I've been told to do since I made my debut, and that's what I'm going to continue doing. The noise has been there since I made my debut, and it will remain for as long as I play. It doesn't really matter too much. What matters is what I do on the field and how I contribute to the success of the team," Rohit said.
Article Summary: Former India head coach and commentator Ravi Shastri has backed Rohit Sharma amid retirement speculation. He has urged the team management to allow the veteran opener to continue playing for as long as he wants. Rohit silenced his critics in emphatic fashion by smashing a magnificent 138 off 110 balls in the third ODI against England at the Home of Cricket.

Article Title: 'His retirement will be decided': Mohammad Kaif makes bold statement on Rohit Sharma's future after Lord's heroics
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma (BCCI Photo)

Kaif urged BCCI to back him

England beat India to clinch ODI series

Former India cricketer and commentator Mohammad Kaif has thrown his weight behind Rohit Sharma amid growing speculation over the international future, insisting that retirement is a personal decision and should not be dictated by public opinion.Rohit recently silenced critics in emphatic fashion by smashing a historic century at Lord's during the 3rd ODI against England. His knock of 138 from 110 balls made him the first Indian batter to score an ODI century at the iconic venue, arriving at a time when rumours had intensified that the Lord's fixture could be his final international appearance before the 2027 ODI World Cup.Those retirement rumours were earlier dismissed by the BCCI, and Rohit himself responded in the best possible way, with the bat.Reacting to the debate surrounding the India captain, Kaif said Rohit has continued to perform despite immense external pressure and deserves the freedom to decide when to call time on his career."Rohit Sharma's retirement will be decided by Rohit Sharma himself. He has the right. He has worked so hard for India. He has the right to retire of his own will. 12,000 runs, 34 centuries - till the time he was the captain, he never let India lose.Not even today was anyone able to defeat India in white-ball cricket under his captaincy. What a captain he has been. Yet there is so much pressure on him, with people constantly saying, 'Rohit Sharma, it's time to retire. ' Under all that pressure, he became the highest run-scorer at Lord's. No other Indian batter scored a century there in this match, it came from Rohit's bat," Kaif said in a video posted on his X account.Kaif further suggested that public backing from the Indian team management and the BCCI could further motivate the veteran opener ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup."Imagine if Shubman Gill, as captain, publicly says, 'Rohit bhai, I need you for the 2027 World Cup.' Or if the BCCI clearly states that Rohit will play for India for as long as he wants and nobody should question him. That kind of support would make a huge difference," he added.The former India batter believes Rohit thrives on responsibility and confidence from those around him."Right now, he is under pressure because everyone is waiting for him to fail. But when he knows his captain, coach and the BCCI are standing firmly behind him, he will even scale the Himalayas for India. I hope people stop the unnecessary noise and allow Rohit Sharma to play in peace," Kaif concluded.India suffered a 27-run defeat to England in the third and final ODI, conceding the three-match series 2-1 despite fighting centuries and half-centuries from their top order. Chasing a daunting 388-run target, captain Rohit Sharma led from the front with a magnificent century, while Shubman Gill chipped in with 77 and Virat Kohli added a fluent 74.However, the massive target proved too steep as India's middle and lower order failed to sustain the momentum.
Article Summary: Kaif urges BCCI to back Rohit Sharma ahead of 2027 ODI World Cup. India suffered 27-run defeat to England in third and final ODI, conceding the three-match series 2-1. Rohit became the first Indian batter to score an ODI century at Lord's.

Article Title: Duleep Trophy 2026-27: West Zone announce star-studded squad, Ruturaj Gaikwad named captain
Article Text:
Ruturaj Gaikwad named captain of West Zone in Duleep Trophy (Image: X)

MUMBAI:

West Zone squad:

In a lifeline to his career which slided down after an initial high, Prithvi Shaw was on Monday picked for the West Zone Duleep Trophy squad following an impressive performance for Maharashtra last domestic season.The squad was announced on Monday following a meeting of the West Zone selection committee, which was chaired by Mumbai's new chief selector Rajesh Pawar.The Duleep Trophy traditionally kicks off the domestic season. Like last season, the competition will be played from Aug 23 to Sept 10 at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence (CoE) grounds in Bengaluru. India opener Yashasvi Jaiswal, who was a part of the West Zone side last year, will of course miss the tournament this time as India will be touring Sri Lanka for a two-Test series during that time, while batter Shreyas Iyer too isn't a part of the squad.Shaw moved to Maharashtra from Mumbai last season, and finished the Ranji Trophy as thw highest run-getter for his new team, scoring 537 runs in seven matches @48.81, with one hundred and three fifties. His highest score was a blazing 156-ball 222 against Chandigarh, a knock during which he smashed the third fastest double century in the history of the Ranji Trophy.The 26-year-old was not picked in the West Zone team for the Duleep Trophy last season after enduring ordinary season for Mumbai during which he was dropped due to poor fitness.“Prithvi scored more than 500 runs for Maharashtra in the Ranji Trophy last year. We all know about his enormous talent. He is still 26 and can still make a comeback to the Indian team one day You never know!,” Rajesh Pawar told TOI.Rated as a highly talented batsman when he started out, Shaw, who made a sensational Test debut when he scored a century (134) against West Indies in 2018 at Rajkot at the age of 18, played the last of his five Tests (339 runs@42.37, including two half-centuries too) at Adelaide (pink-ball Test) in 2020.Meanwhile, seasoned India batter Ruturaj Gaikwad has been named as the captain of the West Zone squad for the upcoming Duleep Trophy, with Mumbai's prolific left-arm spin-bowling all-rounder Shams Mulani will be the vice-captain.
