Article Title: Picture abhi baaki hai! Away from the bell and egg-and-bacon ties, Rohit Sharma keeps his own England tradition alive at Lord's
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma plays a shot during 3rd ODI against England at Lord's. (ANI Photo)

TimesofIndia.com in London:

I think the way Rohit bhai paced his innings was outstanding Shubman Gill

India's Rohit Sharma plays a shot during 3rd ODI against England, at Lord's in London on Sunday. (ANI Photo)

We played our entire career together, so it was nice to have him in the middle. We've had a lot of partnerships. It's always fun batting together. We understand each other so well. Rohit Sharma

Eight years ago, Rohit Sharma summed himself up with a line that now feels almost prophetic: "Throw me to the wolves and I come back leading the pack." As retirement speculation engulfed him ahead of the Lord's ODI, the 39-year-old responded exactly as that quote promised, rising above the chatter with an innings that dismissed every question about his future.On Sunday, Lord's was painted in blue for the third ODI between India and England. There are plenty of traditions that define this iconic venue: the golden-and-red-striped ties, aka the egg-and-bacon tie; the five-minute bell, rung by Yuvraj Singh on this occasion; a walk through the Long Room with the Honours Board on display and the watchful presence of Father Time. Away from all this stood Rohit Sharma. He had been welcomed during the nets session a day prior with plenty of cheers, and it continued as the team arrived for the series decider.Over the last few days, the focus was squarely on the 39-year-old. The third and final ODI was billed as his last. Some reports claimed his parents were in attendance for this milestone. Retirement rumours were circulating. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia needed to officially come out and deny that it was going to be Rohit's last. Yet, it didn't stop the rumour mill from working overtime.As for Rohit, he looked completely at ease in his own skin."Look, my job is with the bat. Come and play, represent my country, represent the team. That's what I've been told to do since my debut, and that's what I'm going to do. The noise, since I made my debut, has been there. And till the time I'm going to stay here, it is always going to be there. So it doesn't really matter too much. What matters is what I do on the field, try and contribute to the success of the team. That's all my focus is right now. And let the noise be there. If there's no noise, there's no fun. My job is inside, their job is outside. That's how I look at it," he told BCCI.tv after the match.And on the field, Rohit did what he's done before in this part of the world.Opening alongside Shubman Gill with a massive 388 runs to chase, Rohit did what he's been doing effortlessly over the past two decades. He toyed with the bowlers while pacing his innings perfectly. A near-run-a-ball 50 became an 84-ball century as the accelerator was pressed after the 70-run mark. The right-hander switched gears swiftly to jump from 69 off 69 to 121 off 100, scoring 52 runs off 31 balls."I think the way Rohit bhai paced his innings was outstanding," skipper Shubman Gill said later. "During the Powerplay, we spoke about whether we should go after the bowling or not, but we know it's not easy to attack against the new ball. The way he paced his innings and then accelerated was exceptional. Once he got into the 60s and 70s, it was truly a treat to watch," he added.Even as Rohit limped while completing singles, with the 30% humidity playing its part, he chose to tonk the bowlers rather than deal in singles and doubles with Virat Kohli at the other end. That 121 off 100 became 132 off 107 following twin boundaries in a Sam Curran over, including a cracking shot towards deep extra cover. Two balls later, Jacob Bethell could only look towards cow corner as Rohit sent the ball flying for a maximum, his fifth of the day. One could see the hapless expression on Bethell's face. It wasn't a bad ball. It was just bowled to an in-form Rohit, who has done this many a time before.The England bowler did get his revenge a ball later as Rohit went for a sweep, missed, and the ball found his pads before crashing into the stumps for a lucky dismissal.Rohit took in the adulation and appreciation of the tens of thousands in attendance. His 34th ODI century. His eighth in England. And the first by an Indian at Lord's. All added to his resume. His impressive and seemingly yet-to-be-finished resume.The other half of the famous RoKo, Virat Kohli , kept the chase alive. The chasemaster believed even as Rohit walked off after their 113-run stand, long after the duo, playing their 400th match together, had shared a massive hug following Rohit's ton. India needed 128 from 68 balls. Was a miracle, a la NatWest 2002, possible?Kohli tried his utmost. A tossed-up Will Jacks delivery allowed the 37-year-old to dance down the track and send it sailing over the bowler's head for a maximum. Still with a job to finish, Kohli barely lifted his bat in acknowledgement of his 46-ball fifty, his first at Lord's. Two balls later, Kohli used his wrists to send the ball over deep backward square leg for yet another six.In between, Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer came and went. Kohli stood in the middle, and a colleague chimed in, "lone warrior again." The gladiator of the Indian team then went after Jacob Bethell, hitting him for a straight six.But the knock, and the chase, were effectively over after Sam Curran got rid of Kohli for 74 off 60 balls, laced with four fours and three sixes. Kohli, as always, was frustrated that he couldn't get the job done and couldn't steer the team past the finish line.With India losing the bilateral ODI series 1-2, having been thrashed 0-2 and 0-4 by Ireland and England, respectively, in the T20Is, there will be plenty for the BCCI hierarchy to assess. But for RoKo, who continue to bring thousands into stadiums and millions to their TV sets, the road is not over."We played our entire career together, so it was nice to have him in the middle. We've had a lot of partnerships. It's always fun batting together. We understand each other so well. It's always nice in the middle, bouncing off ideas and trying to see what we can do. So there was a lot of conversation going on while we were batting," Rohit said about Kohli and their time together in the middle at Lord's.Unless something drastic happens, that time in the middle will continue for at least one more series. Kohli and Rohit had contrasting report cards from this series in their bid to be in South Africa for the 2027 ODI World Cup. While Kohli scored 144 runs from three matches, bouncing back after a blip at Edgbaston, Rohit raced away to 175 runs in the series following his century at Lord's.As for Rohit's retirement rumours and the end of his 19-year ODI career, the snooze button can be swiftly pressed. "He's not told us anything. I think it's all out in the media, but there's not been any discussion like that in the team," skipper Shubman Gill said in the post-match press conference.India's next ODI assignment is in September against the West Indies, with more in store in New Zealand in November and against Sri Lanka in December.
Article Summary: Rohit Sharma scores 121 not out in 3rd ODI against England at Lord's. The 39-year-old dismisses retirement speculation ahead of the series decider. Shubman Gill: "I think the way Rohit bhai paced his innings was outstanding"

Article Title: BFC reserves stay unbeaten during exposure tour of Japan
Article Text: KURATE (JAPAN): Renedy Singh’s Bengaluru FC Reserves finished with an unbeaten run as the Reliance Foundation Development League (RFDL)’s exposure tour of Japan for the league’s top three teams concluded on Monday.BFC held Avispa Fukuoka to a goalless draw before emerging 4-3 winners in the penalty shootout in their final match. Renedy’s side, which won the RFDL 2025-2026 season, had earlier defeated Giravanz Kitakyushu 3-2 and Sagan Tosu 2-0 in their previous two matches.It was, however, heartbreak for Punjab FC who went down FC Baleine Shimonoseki 5-6 in sudden death. The match finished 1-1 in regulation time at Nogihama Park, on the outskirts of Fukuoka city.Following their resounding 5-0 thrashing of Avispa Fukuoka U-18 and 3-1 victory over Giravanz Kitakyushu, Praveen Kumar’s PFC side looked on course for another victory when Singamayum Shami gave them a 38th-minute lead. However, FC Baleine Shimonoseki came to level the scoreline in stoppage time of the second half and then went on to clinch the deal 7-6 via penalty shootout.FC Goa, however, rounded off their campaign with a 3-1 victory over Giravanz Kitakyushu. Malsawmtluanga opened the scoring in the 10th minute to give FC Goa an early advantage before Sojiro equalised shortly after the restart. Goa came back strongly after the break, with Sitroy Carvalho and Shawn Fernandes finding the back of the net in the second half to seal their first win of the tour.RFDL, which has been organizing the league for the past five seasons, started the exposure tour of Japan last week, allowing the league’s top-three finishers to play three matches each here.
Article Summary: Renedy Singh’s Bengaluru FC Reserves finished with an unbeaten run as the Reliance Foundation Development League (RFDL)'s exposure tour of Japan concluded on Monday. Article Title: Why Spain vs Argentina became a FIFA World Cup final to forget
Article Text:
PTI Photo

Argentina’s approach



Spain lacking cutting edge



Messi frustrated



Star battle failing to ignite



Sunday’s title showdown failed to live up to the hype. TOI takes a look at the factors that contributed to a dull contest ...From the outset, the Argentina plan seemed clear: Don’t allow Spain time on the ball and resort to tactical fouls to disrupt their passing rhythm. It led to a one-sided title clash, perhaps best encapsulated by a shocking stat: Argentina became the first-ever team to not have a single shot inside 90 minutes in a World Cup final.As expected, La Roja bossed possession (68%) but for large parts of the game, couldn’t quite convert their dominance into clear-cut goalscoring chances. Rodri remained a key influence in Spain looking to impose their game, but Luis de la Fuente’s side had to remain patient while the holders stuck to their stifling approach.Messi had just 15 touches in the first half and 54 over the game. Spain’s midfield led by Rodri ensured Messi never got the ball in positions to score. His attempts to pass to teammates also didn’t connect.One of the most riveting subplots fans had been waiting to see unravel involved FC Barcelona’s past and present symbols — Lionel Messi v Lamine Yamal. In a final that was crying out for moments of inspiration, neither of them was able to stamp their authority on the game.
Article Summary: Argentina became the first-ever team to not have a single shot inside 90 minutes in a World Cup final. Lionel Messi had just 15 touches in the first half and 54 over the game. La Roja bossed possession (68%) but for large parts of the game, couldn’t convert their dominance into clear-cut goalscoring chances.

Article Title: Luis de la Fuente: The architect behind Spain's FIFA World Cup revival
Article Text:
PTI Photo

Spaniards appear to be particularly skilled at frustrating their opponents. Their PM, Pedro Sanchez, showed this on the geopolitical pitch, annoying Trump repeatedly over his refusal to let US use Spain’s airspace for the Iran war.Weeks later, Luis de la Fuente, head of their national team, expressed similar faith in his ‘camaraderie’ theory to frustrate football’s superpowers — Portugal, Belgium, France and finally the ‘untouchables’, Lionel Messi ’s Argentina. Spain’s World Cup triumph marks the return of a footballing empire — one built not on the brilliance of superstars, but on the power and appeal of the collective.Having conquered Europe in 2024, Spain’s Sunday victory in New York two years later completed a remarkable renaissance, confirming that the country’s football identity had evolved rather than simply returned.The possession-based approach to suffocate the opposition into submission, kicked off by Luis Aragones, had earned Spain their first continental trophy in 2008, after 44 years.Then, they conquered the world in 2010, riding atop Vicente del Bosque’s passing carousel. The European summit re-scaled in 2012 was the high-point, a delicious mix of passing creativity and penalty box sharpness. But then, Spain lost their way in a passing warp.Caught in the maze of possession, Spain wallowed in the quagmire as Del Bosque’s men failed in 2014. In Qatar 2022, enjoying 75% possession, Luis Enrique’s boys failed to score in 120 minutes against Morocco! In walked Luis de la Fuente. As of Sunday, Spain are yet to lose any of their continental clashes since the 65-year old’s appointment, four years ago. La Roja won all seven games to claim the Euro 2024 scoring 15 goals. This time, they won seven out of eight with one draw, scored 14 and conceded just one. Leveraging a decade of nurturing Spain’s youth teams, he used his deep bonds with players he had nourished since their teenage years.Unlike many modern international sides that revolve around one transcendent figure, Spain’s greatest strength was that no player was indispensable. Lamine Yamal dazzled, Rodri controlled, Pedri dictated tempo, Nico Williams stretched defences and Ferran Torres, a substitute, delivered the decisive goal. Yet none of them carried the burden alone. With the fate of the final still precariously poised, Rodri made way for Zubimendi for his first taste of the World Cup in the 99th minute. Ideas over icons.The architect of this resurgence was De la Fuente himself. He coached Spain’s Under-19s to the European title in 2015, the Under-21s to the European Championship in 2019, and the Olympic side to silver in Tokyo before taking charge of the senior team in 2022. Many of the players who lifted the World Cup had already learned his theorems as teenagers. Players arrived in the senior squad fluent in De la Fuente’s language. The national team was simply the latest stage of a long developmental journey.Euro 2024 offered the first glimpse of this transformation. Spain abandoned the stereotype of sterile possession that had come to define the latter years of the Xavi-Iniesta era (2008-2012). They added speed, verticality and athleticism.Lamine Yamal and Nico Williams provided width and acceleration, while Rodri and Pedri ensured control in midfield. The European title was the foundation of a larger project that reached its logical conclusion on Sunday.
Article Summary: Spaniards appear to be particularly skilled at frustrating their opponents. Spain’s World Cup triumph marks the return of a footballing empire. Spain abandoned the stereotype of sterile possession that had come to define the latter years of the Xavi-Iniesta era (2008-2012). They added speed, verticality and athleticism.

Article Title: FIFA World Cup 2026 | Method over madness: How Spain's collective brilliance conquered the world
Article Text:
PTI Photo

It was the kind of Ferrandipity Spain perhaps needed in the end to reclaim their world. When the denouement arrived, the camera slowly turned observational, staying close to a few central characters and showing how they tried to fit into the sense of eventuality. Against the sunny backdrop of a giant New Jersey stadium, a parable of disparate parts took shape, blurring the line of connections between present and past.Nico Williams headed Pedro Porro’s cross back into the middle of the box and Ferran Torres drove home Spain’s march to the summit with a rasping left-footer in the 106th minute, 16 years after Andres Iniesta’s coup de grace with another extra-time winner announced their arrival on the world’s stage. As Ferran, with adrenaline pumping, uprooted the corner flag with a giant kick and was mobbed by teammates in wild celebration, Iniesta seated with his 2010 teammates, came in the frame, clapping and smiling.Playing in counterpoint to this montage of images stood Lionel Messi — his eyes downcast and shoulders hunched, almost dreamily detached, perhaps resigning to the impending inevitability.Spain’s rebirth in the game’s grandest stage coincided with an awful self-destruction of Argentina.No shots were on target in the regulation time; there was no heart in the play-forMessi joie de vivre and a peculiar disregard for making their battle more meaningful, hit an impenetrable barrier.Argentina’s sky was too clouded for their cosmic radiance — El Aleph — to shine and turn inspirational on a dime, and thus, the deus ex machina never came in any form of those stolen moments of ingenuity late in the semifinal against England.Enzo Fernandez’s red card deep into the regulation time came with a maddening jolt when hope was replaced with dread and from which point it became clear where the contest was heading. The winners’ curse predictably struck Argentina again as the end to their title defence came with a more brutal image — Leandro Paredes inviting another red card after being involved in an ugly clash with Eric Garcia and Gavi following the full-time whistle.This is why Spain’s triumph looked so redemptive, almost dripping with poetic justice. It was less of a typical La Furia Roja but more of a symphony in different dazzling hues. Fearlessly methodical, enchantingly expressive and always a deep sense of colectivismo being at the centre of everything.Luis de la Fuente has turned their erstwhile passing lullaby into a more direct and dynamic force, bypassing the crowded midfields through vertical expansion. When syncs between the players were tested and strengthened by great adversity, it carried a lyricism of someone arriving at the point of self-discovery. It felt fluid and free within its thematic bounds so much so that one might be tempted to take Messi’s Argentina as an antagonist in the narrative.In a seemingly stream-ofconsciousness course of their post-match celebration on Sunday, another enduring image stayed. Messi stood up to receive a warm embrace from the 19-year-old Lamine Yamal as the coronation of the champions was beginning. It was a picture unshakably beautiful and moving in its connotation; it was about passing the baton.
Article Summary: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final in New Jersey. Ferran Torres scored the only goal of the game in the 106th minute. Andres Iniesta scored the winning goal for Spain in the 2010 final. Lionel Messi's Argentina were unable to find a winner in the final.

Article Title: Argentina players could face FIFA bans after World Cup 2026 final chaos against Spain
Article Text:
Image credit: X

Heated scenes after the FIFA World Cup final



What punishment could Argentina players face?



FIFA confirms disciplinary investigation



Argentina already under FIFA scrutiny



NEW DELHI: Argentina's World Cup final defeat to Spain could have further consequences, with FIFA launching an investigation into the post-match clashes that broke out after Sunday's final at the New York New Jersey Stadium in New Jersey.Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time to win their second FIFA World Cup title, but celebrations were overshadowed by heated confrontations between players from both teams after the final whistle.Several Argentina players were involved in confrontations during Spain's celebrations. The visuals of the ugly scenes soon went viral on the social media platforms.Leandro Paredes and Thiago Almada were seen wrestling Spain midfielder Gavi to the ground. In another incident, Paredes appeared to grab Spain defender Eric Garcia by the neck.Nahuel Molina also appeared to swing a punch towards Spain midfielder Rodri as he ran to celebrate with his teammates.Veteran defender Nicolas Otamendi was involved in a heated exchange with Rodri over comments reportedly made by Spain defender Aymeric Laporte before the final. Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala clashed with Spain midfielder Dani Olmo.Under Article 14 of the FIFA Disciplinary Code, players found guilty of violent conduct face a minimum three-match suspension.The same minimum ban also applies for offences involving: assault, elbowing, punching, kicking, biting, spitting, hitting an opponent or any person other than a match official.Any suspension would apply when Argentina next plays official matches.Apart from player bans, the Argentine Football Association (AFA) could also face disciplinary action if FIFA concludes that the national team behaved improperly. Players and officials may also be fined, while FIFA can impose additional sanctions if required.FIFA announced that it has appointed a prosecutor to examine the incidents after reviewing the match reports.In a statement, FIFA said: "Following an assessment of the relevant match reports for the FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, and in line with Article 36 of the FIFA Disciplinary Code (FDC), the FIFA Disciplinary Committee has appointed a Disciplinary and Ethics Prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of the FDC with regard to the post-match incidents."Further details will be communicated by the FIFA Disciplinary Committee once the prosecutor's report has been completed."The World Cup finalists are already facing another possible disciplinary case linked to their 2-1 semi-final win over England. After that match, several Argentina players displayed a banner reading: "Las Malvinas son Argentinas". The slogan translates to "The Falklands are Argentine."
Article Summary: FIFA confirms disciplinary investigation into Argentina's World Cup final defeat. Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time to win their second FIFA World Cup title. Celebrations were overshadowed by heated confrontations between players from both teams. Players found guilty of violent conduct face a minimum three-match suspension.

Article Title: 'The pain is immense': Lionel Messi pens emotional note after Argentina lose FIFA World Cup 2026 final to Spain
Article Text:
Lionel Messi (PTI Photo)

How Spain ended Argentina's reign



NEW DELHI: Lionel Messi shared an emotional message after Argentina's 0-1 defeat to Spain in the FIFA World Cup 2026 final at the New York New Jersey Stadium on Sunday. While admitting that the loss was painful, the 39-year-old said he was proud of what Argentina had achieved during their title defence.Spain ended Argentina's hopes of becoming the first team in 64 years to successfully defend the FIFA World Cup . Substitute Ferran Torres scored the only goal in the 106th minute of extra time to hand La Roja their second World Cup title.Taking to Instagram after the final, Messi thanked Argentina's supporters and said the team should still be proud of reaching back-to-back World Cup finals."The pain is immense, and this wound will take time to heal. But I also hold onto all the good things... The matches we turned around by giving it our all - moments that will remain in our memories forever - and the support of an entire country which, combined with this group's hard work and effort, brought us back among the world's elite once again. It is hard to fully appreciate our achievement right now, but this group reached two consecutive World Cup finals," Messi wrote."Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and message.Once again, we managed to unite as a country and stand together, sharing the immense pride of being Argentine," he said."I also want to congratulate Spain on winning the championship," Messi added.Despite the heartbreak, the mood in Buenos Aires reflected pride, with fans applauding a team that reached another World Cup final and fought until the very end.Torres scored his first goal of the FIFA World Cup 2026 at the biggest moment of all, coming off the bench to fire Spain to a 1-0 extra-time victory over Argentina and restore La Roja to the top of world football.The substitute struck in the 106th minute, denying Lionel Messi a second straight World Cup title in what the Argentine captain has indicated was his final appearance at the tournament.Torres reacted quickest to a bouncing ball inside the penalty area and smashed a left-footed shot just under the crossbar to seal Spain's second World Cup title after their triumph in 2010.
Article Summary: Lionel Messi says he is proud of what Argentina achieved during their title defence. Argentina lost 0-1 to Spain in the FIFA World Cup 2026 final on Sunday. Substitute Ferran Torres scored the only goal in the 106th minute of extra time to hand La Roja their second World Cup title.

Article Title: Why Marc Cucurella buried coin in pitch before Spain's World Cup final as 'secret' 2010 ritual comes to light
Article Text:
Marc Cucurella’s secret pre-match ritual helped continue Spain’s World Cup-winning superstition/ Image:X

The 'secret' lucky coin tradition

Spain's lucky charm ends with another World Cup

Capdevila's own World Cup journey almost ended before it began

Marc Cucurella was spotted carrying out an unusual pre-match ritual moments before Spain's FIFA World Cup 2026 final against Argentina, and it has now emerged that the act was part of a 16-year-old superstition passed down by one of Spain's previous World Cup winners.Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 after extra time at the New York New Jersey Stadium to lift the men's World Cup for the second time in their history, with substitute Ferran Torres scoring the decisive goal in the 106th minute.While much of the attention after the final centred on Spain's triumph and Argentina's late collapse, footage captured shortly before kick-off revealed Cucurella quietly walking towards the touchline, removing an object from his sock and burying it beneath the turf.Initially, nobody knew what the Spain left-back had hidden in the grass.The mystery was solved after the final by former Spain defender Joan Capdevila, who revealed that the object was a coin and that he had personally asked Cucurella to continue a superstition dating back to Spain's first World Cup triumph in 2010.Capdevila, who started at left-back when Spain defeated the Netherlands in the 2010 World Cup final in Johannesburg, explained that he had buried a coin in the pitch before that match and encouraged Cucurella to repeat the ritual before facing Argentina.Writing on X, Capdevila said: "And now I'll tell you a secret... In 2010, I buried a coin in the grass before starting the match... I've told it millions of times."I asked @cucurella3 to do the same yesterday..."Marc, I love you so much. YOU ARE A WORLD CHAMPION!"He also shared the video showing Cucurella discreetly checking that nobody was watching before placing the coin into the turf and covering it with grass moments before kick-off.Whether coincidence or superstition, the ritual appeared to work once again.Spain controlled much of the final against defending champions Argentina before finally finding the breakthrough in extra time.Ferran Torres struck in the 106th minute after being set up by Nico Williams, handing Luis de la Fuente's side a hard-earned 1-0 victory and securing Spain's second World Cup title, exactly 16 years after their first.Cucurella was once again a key figure throughout the tournament, capping another successful international campaign after helping Spain win the European Championship two years earlier.Argentina's hopes of forcing penalties had already suffered a major blow when Enzo Fernández was sent off in stoppage time of normal time after receiving a second yellow card for a reckless challenge on Pau Cubarsí. Tempers later boiled over after the final whistle, with Leandro Paredes also being dismissed following an altercation involving several Spain players.The story carried extra significance because Capdevila himself almost missed the final.Earlier in the week, the 2010 World Cup winner revealed that his Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA) application to enter the United States had been denied, reportedly because of a previous exhibition match he had played in Iran.Capdevila publicly appealed to US President Donald Trump on social media, writing: "I NEED HELP @realDonaldTrump!""They just told me that I can't travel to the final with my kids because my ESTA has been denied."Can anyone help me with this? You have no idea how excited I was to be there with all my 2010 teammates and this team to cheer them on."I can't believe they're not letting me into the USA... and that I'll miss a moment like this with my kids who love soccer so much."According to ESPN, US Customs and Border Protection later confirmed to the Associated Press that it had received a request regarding Capdevila's case and subsequently granted him permission to enter the country.The former Villarreal defender arrived in New Jersey in time for the final and watched Spain lift the World Cup from the stands.After the victory, he celebrated both Spain's triumph and his own successful journey by posting: "HOW WASN'T IT WORTH IT... I DESERVED TO BE HERE WITH MY FAMILY ENJOYING THIS MOMENT, AND JUSTICE HAS BEEN SERVED. Thanks to everyone who pushed for this to be possible, thanks to all of you from the bottom of my heart."For Capdevila, the coin buried beneath the grass had already brought Spain luck once in 2010. Sixteen years later, after Cucurella repeated the same quiet ritual before kick-off, it ended with another World Cup trophy heading back to Spain.
Article Summary: Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the FIFA World Cup 2026 final. Substitute Ferran Torres scored the decisive goal in the 106th minute. Marc Cucurella was spotted carrying out an unusual pre-match ritual. The act was part of a 16-year-old superstition passed down by one of Spain's previous World Cup winners.
